I am organizing my research on federated learning and need to set up a knowledge base. Please search for papers about federated learning from the academic literature repository and organize them in two ways.

First, create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Federated Learning Research Hub". Inside this page, create a child database called "Paper Index" that contains an entry for each federated learning paper. Each entry should include the paper title, authors, and a short summary.

Second, create an Excel file called "Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx" in my workspace. It should have two sheets. The first sheet "Paper Details" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, and Abstract_Length (the character count of the abstract). The second sheet "Summary" should have columns Metric and Value, listing Total_Papers (the number of papers found), Avg_Abstract_Length (the average character count of all abstracts rounded to the nearest integer), Earliest_Year, and Latest_Year.

Please include all papers that are related to federated learning, including foundational papers about federated approaches and surveys of the field.

Note on the spreadsheet: write all numeric values (Abstract_Length and every Summary metric) as literal numbers in the cells. Do not rely on Excel formulas for these values, since formulas are not computed by the reading tool. Compute the values yourself (e.g. with your code tool) and fill in the resulting numbers.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 sub-agent for the following numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own complete read-only paper discovery. Issue complementary task-derived federated-learning queries to the local arXiv search at its supported per-call result bound, union and deduplicate the returned records by stable ID, and retain every genuinely relevant result including foundational and survey work. Because the search exposes no cursor or list-all operation, do not claim coverage beyond this observed query union. Preserve full title, complete authors, abstract, published date/year, and abstract character count, and return the normalized union directly with per-query/union/retained counts, IDs, year range, and abstract-length controls. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Notion or Excel state.

After Wave 1, the main agent must verify the complementary-query controls and deduplicated observed union, determine the related-paper count only from returned records, and freeze literal summary metrics and one title/author/summary record per retained paper using only task-visible runtime evidence.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Notion hierarchy exclusively. Search for an existing Federated Learning Research Hub, create at most one parent page, then create exactly one Paper Index child database under that returned parent and add one entry per frozen paper with title, authors, and a source-faithful short summary. Keep the whole create-parent → create-database → populate → read-back sequence in this agent. Return page/database IDs, entry count, covered IDs/titles, and validation. Do not write Excel.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx exclusively. Create exactly Paper Details and Summary with the exact required headers, one row per frozen paper, literal numeric abstract lengths and metrics, and the rounded average, earliest year, and latest year. Read back both sheets and return path, row counts, summary values, and header/value validation. Do not modify Notion.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile paper IDs, counts, authors, and summary metrics across the Notion database and workbook, verify both external state and file integrity, and then complete without adding unrelated papers or extra deliverables.

nodes.text:
You are a read-only academic-literature researcher. Your job is to discover papers about federated learning from the local arXiv search tool (mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers) and return a normalized, deduplicated union of records. DO NOT write any files, and DO NOT create any Notion pages or Excel workbooks — you are strictly read-only. The main agent will use your returned records as the frozen dataset for downstream deliverables.

GOAL
Find every genuinely relevant paper about federated learning, including foundational papers about federated approaches (e.g., McMahan et al. "Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data" — the FedAvg paper) and surveys of the field (e.g., "Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning", "A Survey on Federated Learning", etc.), plus other federated-learning-related research.

METHOD (do all of this)
1. Run a set of COMPLEMENTARY, task-derived queries against mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers. Use each query with its supported result bound (use max_results: 50 where possible). Suggested queries (you may adjust wording, but keep them complementary and covering):
   - "federated learning"
   - "federated learning" ANDNOT "survey"  (to surface non-survey work if the union is dominated by surveys)
   - ti:"federated learning"  (title search)
   - "federated learning" AND ("survey" OR "foundations")
   - "federated" AND "privacy"  (if relevant results appear)
   - abs:"federated learning"
   Use category filters like ["cs.LG", "cs.AI", "cs.DC"] and/or date filters only if they help relevance; prefer broad coverage.
2. Collect ALL returned records from every query. UNION and DEDUPLICATE by stable ID (arXiv ID, e.g., 1602.05629).
3. Retain every record that is genuinely relevant to federated learning (federated approaches, federated optimization, federated surveys, federated privacy/security, federated applications). Do not retain obviously unrelated results. Keep foundational and survey work.
4. For each retained paper, capture: paper ID (arXiv id), FULL title, COMPLETE author list (as returned), the full abstract text, the published date/year, and the abstract character count (length of the abstract string, counting characters including spaces — compute it yourself, e.g., len(abstract) if you had code; otherwise count carefully).

NOTE ON COVERAGE: The search tool exposes no cursor or list-all operation, so your coverage is limited to the observed union of your queries. Do NOT claim to cover the entire corpus. Just report what you observed. Do not guess or hallucinate papers — only include records actually returned by the search tool.

DELIVERABLE — return a structured report containing:
1. Per-query summary: for each query, the number of results returned and how many were retained.
2. Union/retained counts: total unique records in the union, how many were deduplicated (duplicates found), and final retained count.
3. The normalized union: a list of ALL retained papers, each with: paper_id, title, authors (full list), abstract (full text), year, abstract_length (integer character count).
4. Controls: the full list of retained paper IDs, the year range (min and max year), and the abstract-length min/max values (so the main agent can sanity-check).
5. Any notes on relevance judgment for borderline records.

Be thorough and complete — every retained paper must be in the final list with all fields. Do not truncate the abstract text. Format the final list as structured text (e.g., one block per paper with labeled fields) so the main agent can parse it reliably.
Discover federated learning papers

You are an external-workflow operator responsible EXCLUSIVELY for the Notion knowledge-base hierarchy. Do NOT create or modify any Excel files, and do NOT touch the local filesystem except as needed for nothing — your deliverable is purely in Notion. Use the mcp__notion__* tools.

CONTEXT / FROZEN DATASET (already verified by the main agent — use exactly this; do not re-derive, add, or drop papers):
4 federated learning papers, each with title, authors, and year:
1. id=1602.05629, title="Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data", authors="H. Brendan McMahan, Eider Moore, Daniel Ramage, Seth Hampson, Blaise Agüera y Arcas", year=2016
2. id=1812.06127, title="Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks", authors="Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Manzil Zaheer, Maziar Sanjabi, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith", year=2018
3. id=1908.07873, title="Federated Learning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions", authors="Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith", year=2019
4. id=1912.04977, title="Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning", authors="Peter Kairouz, H. Brendan McMahan, Brendan Avent, Aurélien Bellet, Mehdi Bennis", year=2019

SHORT SUMMARIES (source-faithful, one per paper — write these into the database entries):
1. 1602.05629: "Introduces federated learning, a decentralized approach that trains a shared model by aggregating locally-computed updates on privacy-sensitive mobile data; presents iterative model averaging (FedAvg) with extensive empirical evaluation showing 10-100x reduction in communication rounds versus synchronized SGD."
2. 1812.06127: "Proposes FedProx, a re-parametrization of FedAvg that adds a proximal term to the local subproblem to handle heterogeneity in federated networks, with convergence guarantees and more robust, fair convergence relative to FedAvg."
3. 1908.07873: "A survey discussing the unique characteristics and challenges of federated learning, providing a broad overview of current approaches in distributed optimization, systems design, and statistical learning, and outlining future research directions."
4. 1912.04977: "A comprehensive survey of federated learning covering recent advances, the principles of focused data collection and minimization, and an extensive collection of open problems and challenges facing the field."

STEPS (keep the entire sequence in this agent; do not hand off):
1. SEARCH: Call mcp__notion__API-post-search with query "Federated Learning Research Hub" to check whether a page with that title already exists. If an existing page with exactly this title (object type "page") is found, REUSE it as the parent (do NOT create a second one). If none exists, create at most ONE new parent page titled "Federated Learning Research Hub" using mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent type "workspace" (or a page_id parent only if you find an obvious team root page to nest under — if you create it, prefer a top-level workspace page). Record the parent page id.
2. CREATE DATABASE: Create exactly ONE child database under that parent page titled "Paper Index" using mcp__notion__API-create-a-database with parent.page_id = the parent page id. Its properties schema must be:
   - "Title": { "type": "title" }  (property name can be "Title" or "Paper Title" — use "Title")
   - "Authors": { "type": "rich_text" }
   - "Summary": { "type": "rich_text" }
   Record the database id.
3. POPULATE: For each of the 4 papers, create one page in the database via mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent.database_id = database id, and properties containing the title (in the title property), Authors (rich_text), and Summary (rich_text) exactly as given above. One entry per paper, 4 entries total.
4. READ BACK & VALIDATE: Query the database (mcp__notion__API-post-database-query) to confirm exactly 4 entries exist and each contains the correct title/authors/summary. Also verify the parent page and database exist (retrieve page / database). Fix anything that is wrong (e.g., a duplicate entry or missing property) so the final state has exactly 4 entries.

RETURN a structured report with:
- parent page id + title
- database id + title
- entry count (must be 4)
- the list of covered paper IDs and titles as stored in Notion
- validation results (what you read back and confirmed)
- any issues encountered and how they were resolved
Build Notion research hub

You are an office-report-builder responsible EXCLUSIVELY for creating one Excel workbook: Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-federated-learning-notion/workspace (full path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-federated-learning-notion/workspace/Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx). Use the mcp__excel__* tools and/or mcp__filesystem__ tools only to create/verify this file. Do NOT create or modify any Notion pages or databases.

CONTEXT / FROZEN DATASET (already verified by the main agent — use exactly this; do not re-derive, add, or drop anything):
4 federated learning papers (Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Abstract_Length[character count of the abstract, computed by the main agent]):
1. 1602.05629 | Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data | H. Brendan McMahan, Eider Moore, Daniel Ramage, Seth Hampson, Blaise Agüera y Arcas | 2016 | 1230
2. 1812.06127 | Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks | Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Manzil Zaheer, Maziar Sanjabi, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith | 2018 | 744
3. 1908.07873 | Federated Learning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions | Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith | 2019 | 601
4. 1912.04977 | Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning | Peter Kairouz, H. Brendan McMahan, Brendan Avent, Aurélien Bellet, Mehdi Bennis | 2019 | 642

FROZEN SUMMARY METRICS:
- Total_Papers = 4
- Avg_Abstract_Length = 804 (rounded nearest integer of (1230+744+601+642)/4 = 804.25)
- Earliest_Year = 2016
- Latest_Year = 2019

STEPS:
1. Create the workbook at the exact path above using mcp__excel__create_workbook.
2. Ensure there is a worksheet named "Paper Details" (create/rename as needed; remove the default sheet if it is named differently so the workbook contains exactly the two required sheets). Write to "Paper Details" starting at A1:
   Header row: Paper_ID | Title | Authors | Year | Abstract_Length
   Then one row per paper (4 rows) with the frozen values. IMPORTANT: Year, and Abstract_Length must be written as LITERAL NUMBERS (integers), NOT as Excel formulas (no "=" prefix). Do the same for nothing else — Title and Authors are text, Paper_ID is text.
3. Create/ensure a second worksheet named "Summary". Write to it starting at A1:
   Header row: Metric | Value
   Rows:
   Total_Papers | 4
   Avg_Abstract_Length | 804
   Earliest_Year | 2016
   Latest_Year | 2019
   All Value cells must be literal numbers, not formulas.
4. READ BACK both sheets (mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel or get_workbook_metadata) and verify: exactly two sheets with the exact names "Paper Details" and "Summary"; correct headers; 4 data rows in Paper Details; the 4 metric rows in Summary; every numeric cell is a number (not a formula string); values match the frozen data above.

RETURN a structured report with:
- full file path
- sheet names and row counts
- the values read back from both sheets (headers + all rows) as evidence
- validation results (header/value checks, confirmation that numbers are literal and not formulas)
- any issues encountered and how they were resolved
Build Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx
